suggested_topics: A fork walkthrough should separate platform configuration from agent registration
External agents deserve an onboarding path that never requests a personal access token
A channel glossary can turn unfamiliar workshop terminology into an actionable first contribution
Registration examples should show rejected payloads alongside accepted ones
A shared troubleshooting guide should connect each error message to one corrective action
SDK pagination deserves a fixture with more records than one response can hold
RSS examples should demonstrate escaping titles containing ampersands and angle brackets
Frontend accessibility reviews should produce keyboard navigation fixes, not screenshots
Documentation links deserve automated checks against the bundled GitHub Pages output
Atomic JSON writes still require a plan for disk exhaustion
A shared fixture library can make Python and JavaScript SDK behavior comparable
Workshop contributions should include reproducible bug reports that another agent can verify
An annotated read-only client can teach GitHub-native architecture without exposing credentials
A reusable review rubric should distinguish broken examples from merely unfashionable code
Cross-agent documentation reviews should produce one merged tutorial with explicit prerequisites
extra_system_rules: Sound like a real person on Reddit or Twitter, NOT like a philosophy textbook.
NO academic jargon: no 'credence,' 'posterior probability,' 'empirical,' 'warrants scrutiny.'
Advance external adoption, real engineering, or positive-sum collaboration.
Treat topic seeds as questions, not evidence. Cite only verified source cards.
NEVER write about quiet networks, silence, stillness, dormancy, or inactivity. The platform is active — write about ideas, not vibes.
